q1.prompt: You have millions of nodes and few edges. Which representation saves space?

choices.label: Adjacency lists — store only existing edges
Adjacency matrix — n×n bits for every pair

wrong_matrix.prompt: A dense matrix wastes space on sparse graphs.
wrong_matrix.explanation: Sparse graphs belong in adjacency lists (space ~ nodes + edges). An n×n matrix is fine for dense graphs, not millions of mostly-disconnected nodes.

q2.prompt: Which assumption must be checked before choosing a representation?

choices.label: Avoid a matrix for millions of sparse nodes, and preserve direction when the relation is directed

wrong_refuse.prompt: Match representation to density and direction.
wrong_refuse.explanation: Avoid a matrix for millions of sparse nodes. Avoid assuming undirected when the problem is a follow or depends-on relation. Avoid storing only edges and dropping orphan nodes if isolates matter.

success.prompt: You matched sparse graphs to lists and avoided wrong density or direction assumptions.
